changelog: V2: fixed edge_2, edge_4, edge_5, edge_7; simplicity 100 -> 50; score 9000 -> 9250 (+250)

lessons.text: Strip surrounding whitespace (including tabs and \r\n) before matching, and allow one or more spaces or tabs between fields instead of a single literal space.
Compare level names case-insensitively, allow optional spaces inside the brackets, map aliases such as WARNING to WARN, and keep an optional/empty trailing message valid.
Validate numeric ranges (month, day, hour, minute, second) inside one precise regular expression and return the spec's default value instead of raising, which keeps functions small.

versions.critique:
The pattern is too literal. (1) It only accepts single spaces between fields; the spec allows one or
more spaces or tabs, so edge_2 fails. Use [ \t]+ between DATE, TIME and [LEVEL]. (2) It requires
"[LEVEL]" with no inner whitespace; the spec allows optional spaces/tabs inside the brackets
(edge_4). Use \[[ \t]*(\w+)[ \t]*\]. (3) It never checks ranges, so hour 24 is accepted (edge_5).
Validate month 01-12, day 01-31, hour 00-23, minute and second 00-59. (4) It requires a space and
then a message after "]", so a line ending at "[INFO]" returns None instead of message "" (edge_7).
Make the message part (.*) follow the bracket directly and strip it. Use fullmatch on the stripped
line.

All behaviour is now correct. The remaining problem is structure: parse_log_line has cyclomatic
complexity 10 because it chains several if statements with "or" range checks, int conversions and
a separate WARNING branch. Move the range validation into the regular expression itself
(month (0[1-9]|1[0-2]), day (0[1-9]|[12][0-9]|3[01]), hour ([01][0-9]|2[0-3]), minute and second
[0-5][0-9]) and use [0-9] instead of \d so only ASCII digits match. Then the function only needs
to: check the type, fullmatch the stripped line, normalise the level (WARNING -> WARN) and check it
against the allowed set. Keep the returned keys exactly the same.

 import re
 
 LEVELS = {"DEBUG", "INFO", "WARN", "ERROR", "CRITICAL"}
-PATTERN = re.compile(r"^(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}) (\d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2}) \[(\w+)\] (.*)$")
+PATTERN = re.compile(
+    r"(\d{4})-(\d{2})-(\d{2})[ \t]+(\d{2}):(\d{2}):(\d{2})[ \t]+\[[ \t]*(\w+)[ \t]*\](.*)",
+    re.DOTALL,
+)
 
 
 def parse_log_line(line: str) -> dict | None:
     if not isinstance(line, str):
         return None
-    match = PATTERN.match(line.strip())
+    match = PATTERN.fullmatch(line.strip())
     if not match:
         return None
-    date, time, level, message = match.groups()
-    level = level.upper().replace("WARNING", "WARN")
+    year, month, day, hour, minute, second, level, message = match.groups()
+    if not 1 <= int(month) <= 12 or not 1 <= int(day) <= 31:
+        return None
+    if int(hour) > 23 or int(minute) > 59 or int(second) > 59:

+    }
